summary: Draft watchdog sibling record. `Win32CalloutWatchdogBugcheckEnabled` sits under the same `Session Manager\\Power` lane as the validated watchdog timeout pair, is absent by default on the clean baseline, has a later current-build Unicode string hit in `ntoskrnl.exe`, and already appears as an adjacent sibling in the watchdog runtime package. The lane is strong enough for packaging as a draft research record, but it still lacks a current-build caller chain, exact live read proof, and any trustworthy non-default value semantics.

setting.name: Win32 Callout Watchdog Bugcheck Enabled
setting.casual_explanation: This appears to be a low-level watchdog-related value under Session Manager Power. On the current clean baseline, the parent key exists but the value is not configured.
setting.why_people_change_it: Kernel and power researchers may inspect this value when tracing watchdog behavior around Session Manager power initialization and callout handling.
setting.tradeoffs_overview: The value is kernel-adjacent, boot-relevant, and currently unproven as an end-user tweak. Evidence is good enough to keep it in the research queue, but not good enough to apply or recommend. The next step is structural proof of the caller path, not a speculative write.
setting.professional_notes: The current repo evidence says `HKLM\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Control\\Session Manager\\Power\\Win32CalloutWatchdogBugcheckEnabled` is absent by default on the clean baseline while the parent path exists. A later targeted current-build string batch found an exact Unicode hit in `C:\\Windows\\System32\\ntoskrnl.exe`. The lightweight watchdog runtime package also carried this value as an adjacent sibling while probing `WatchdogResumeTimeout` and `WatchdogSleepTimeout`, which makes it the strongest un-packaged watchdog sibling candidate. No current-build caller, explicit type contract, or runtime read proof has been established yet.

evidence.title: Net-new power existence probe for Session Manager Power siblings
evidence.summary: The clean baseline batch confirmed that `HKLM\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Control\\Session Manager\\Power` exists while `Win32CalloutWatchdogBugcheckEnabled` is absent by default.

evidence.title: Current-build string hit for Win32CalloutWatchdogBugcheckEnabled
evidence.summary: The broad current-build string batch found an exact Unicode hit for `Win32CalloutWatchdogBugcheckEnabled` in `C:\\Windows\\System32\\ntoskrnl.exe`, which confirms that the current kernel still carries the value name.

evidence.title: Lightweight watchdog runtime packaging kept the sibling in the active lane
evidence.summary: The later watchdog runtime package listed `Win32CalloutWatchdogBugcheckEnabled` as an adjacent sibling while probing the validated watchdog timeout pair, which ties the candidate to the active watchdog lane even though the exact runtime read still failed.

decision.why: The candidate is real enough for a schema-backed draft: it has baseline path/value evidence, a current-build kernel string hit, and adjacency to the already-validated watchdog timeout lane. It is not ready for a validated record because the current-build caller chain, exact runtime read, documented semantics, and safe non-default value mapping are still missing.
